finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: Marshal.load on attacker-supplied base64 data from the `state` parameter allows arbitrary object instantiation and typically remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.
finding.source: POST /restore, params[:state] (any remote client, no authentication)

trace.note: Route POST /restore is exposed with no auth
params[:state] is base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load
Deserialized object is inspected, so gadget methods like inspect/to_s/hash may also be triggered

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no signature/HMAC on the payload, no class allowlist, no use of safe formats; Sinatra's default protections (Rack::Protection) do not mitigate this. No other files exist in the repo.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-6 exposes POST /restore with no authentication and passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load, with no signature, class allowlist or rescue, and app.rb:7 calls inspect on the result; app.rb is the only file in the directory.
